title: HyCAN-DB: Hydrogen in Carbon Nanomaterials Database
description:
An open database of primary hydrogen sorption measurements on carbon sorbents (activated carbons, nanotubes, graphene-family, carbide-derived, templated and doped carbons), built under a publicly registered protocol (10.5281/zenodo.23719010): 17,061 measurement rows from 124 papers (1987–2026) with full per-row provenance, 80 papers drawn as a stratified probability sample of a 5,251-record frame and independently dual-extracted with adjudication, released extraction-agreement statistics, and a 60-row author audit (0 errors).

Registered analyses: at the 77 K excess-uptake maximum the Chahine rule holds on average (ratio to A_BET/500 = 0.98, 95% CI 0.91–1.05, inside the registered ±15% margin; restricted to explicitly stated excess values the interval crosses the margin and the decision is inconclusive). The rule is a poor sample-level predictor (95% prediction interval 0.61–1.56), fails at 1 bar (ratio 0.58), and uptake rises sublinearly with area (ln–ln slope 0.75). Interlaboratory CV on identical commercial carbons is ≈9% for 1-bar uptake. This version supersedes v0.1, whose analyses are withdrawn on its record.
